target.statement: A natural-number sequence tending to infinity, with uniformly bounded one-step upward increments, cannot permanently avoid divisibility by an indexed tail of fresh pairwise-coprime moduli.

nearest_prior_work: The Jacobsthal-function literature studies the maximal gaps between integers coprime to a fixed product, exactly the static forbidden-block object created in the proof.

Ford-Green-Konyagin-Maynard-Tao (2018), Section 1 and Lemma 1.1, encode a residue-class cover of an interval and use the Chinese remainder theorem to translate it into a consecutive block whose entries share prescribed small prime factors.
Hildebrand (1987), Section 4, equations (4.1) and the congruences immediately following, uses pairwise-coprime moduli and CRT to impose divisibility on a fixed tuple of translated offsets.
classification.attribution: Describe the mechanism as the classical Chinese-remainder forbidden-block construction, with Jacobsthal and covering-congruence theory as the nearest literature family. Credit the local work for isolating and formally verifying the time-indexed first-crossing corollary, not for inventing the underlying number theory.
classification.mathematical_interest: The result is elementary in proof depth but genuinely useful in scope: it converts an unbounded supply of fresh divisibility obstructions into a dynamical no-go theorem without assuming monotonicity or coprimality between a modulus and every later state.
classification.reusable_scope: Any recurrence or process that emits fresh pairwise-coprime moduli which divide no later state can invoke the same barrier. The reciprocal-tail dynamics for Erdos 243 are one consumer rather than the theorem's identity.
classification.why_it_matters: The correct public story is a clean reusable abstraction and formalisation of a classical CRT mechanism. Calling it novel mathematics would inflate an elementary corollary; hiding it as routine plumbing would miss its cross-problem value.

primary_sources.title: Uber eine zahlentheoretische Funktion von Jacobsthal
primary_sources.author: Hans-Joachim Kanold
primary_sources.exact_anchor: Opening definition: Jacobsthal's g(n) is the maximum distance between consecutive positive integers coprime to n; the paper then studies this forbidden-gap function for squarefree products.
primary_sources.supports: The established name and literature family for static consecutive blocks avoiding coprimality to a product.
primary_sources.does_not_support: It does not state the time-indexed bounded-rise theorem.

primary_sources.title: Long gaps between primes
primary_sources.venue: Journal of the American Mathematical Society 31 (2018), 65-105
primary_sources.exact_anchor: Section 1, Lemma 1.1: residue classes a_p mod p cover an interval [y]; CRT chooses m congruent to -a_p mod p, making each m+t in the interval divisible by a selected p. The adjacent paragraph identifies Jacobsthal's j as the maximal gap between integers coprime to a product.
primary_sources.supports: The exact static CRT residue-cover to forbidden-consecutive-block mechanism used by the Lean theorem.
primary_sources.does_not_support: It does not formulate the subsequent first-crossing argument for a bounded-rise sequence.

primary_sources.title: The divisor function at consecutive integers
primary_sources.author: Adolf Hildebrand
primary_sources.exact_anchor: Section 4, printed pages 312-313: after imposing pairwise coprimality in condition (*), the congruences n_0 = -a_i mod m_i are solved by CRT, so each translated offset n_0+a_i has its assigned divisor m_i.
primary_sources.supports: A primary-source instance of assigning distinct offsets to pairwise-coprime divisibility moduli by CRT.
primary_sources.does_not_support: Its analytic theorem and tuple construction are otherwise unrelated to the dynamic no-go result.

mechanism_comparison.classical_static_step: Choose B tail moduli and solve x+r = 0 mod m_r for 0 <= r < B. This makes an arbitrarily high block of B consecutive forbidden values.
mechanism_comparison.local_dynamic_step: Because u tends to infinity, take the first time it reaches x+B. The previous value cannot lie in the forbidden block and is therefore below x; the bound u_(n+1) <= u_n+B then prevents the crossing.
mechanism_comparison.strict_delta: The time-indexed nondivisibility hypotheses and one-sided, nonmonotone first-crossing packaging are the local abstraction. The CRT block itself and its relation to Jacobsthal/covering congruences are classical.
mechanism_comparison.scope_sharpening: Pairwise coprimality is a clean sufficient CRT compatibility condition, not a demonstrated necessary condition. The theorem intentionally makes no assertion for arbitrary non-coprime moduli.
